question: True or false: most deep floats set adrift in the boundary current off Labrador rode it south along the North American coast?
answer: False. Bower and colleagues tracked floats released in the deep current off Labrador, and few stayed in it: most peeled off into the open ocean, looping through eddies on their way south. The tidy picture of a deep conveyor belt hugging the coast had been drawn largely from instruments moored along that very coast.
move: An instrument placed on the expected route will find the expected route.
trap: Trusting the conveyor-belt picture, drawn from instruments on the coastal route.
reference: Bower et al., Interior pathways of the North Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, Nature, 2009
